international.headline: India chairs the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
facts: The 18th BRICS Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on September 12–13, 2026, with India as chair.
The 2026 theme was “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
The notes list 11 full members in 2026: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia.
The notes identify 10 partner countries: Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.

BRICS focuses on economic and political cooperation, trade and investment, peace and security, sustainable development, energy, agriculture, health, science and technology, and Global South interests.
The notes state that India held the BRICS Presidency in 2012, 2016, 2021 and 2026.
international.summary: India chaired the 18th BRICS Summit, bringing member states together under a theme centred on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability.
international.staticLink: The first BRIC Summit was held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009; South Africa joined the grouping in 2011.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 18th BRICS Summit took place in New Delhi on September 12–13, 2026, under India’s chairmanship.
international.mainsAngle: Evaluate BRICS as a platform for cooperation and the advancement of Global South interests.
international.apLink: India hosted the summit in New Delhi; no further AP-specific connection is stated.

- **Edition:** **18th BRICS Summit**

- **When:** **September 12–13, 2026**
- **Chair:** **India**
- **Theme:** “**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**”
| Category | Countries |
|---|---|

# 2. Focus and background
- **Focus:** **Economic and political cooperation; trade and investment; peace and security; sustainable development; energy; agriculture; health; science and technology; Global South interests**

international.headline: BRICS members unanimously adopt the Delhi Declaration
facts: The 18th BRICS Summit unanimously adopted the Delhi Declaration.
The declaration supports dialogue and diplomacy in dispute resolution and opposes unilateral wars.
It also addresses the promotion of local currencies, reform of global governance and stronger economic and strategic cooperation.
international.summary: The Delhi Declaration records shared BRICS positions on diplomacy, global governance and economic cooperation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The Delhi Declaration was unanimously adopted at the 18th BRICS Summit.
international.mainsAngle: Consider the declaration’s emphasis on multilateral dialogue, local currencies and reform of global governance.
international.apLink: India hosted the summit in New Delhi; no further AP-specific connection is stated.
international.notes:
# 1. Declaration adopted
- **What:** **Delhi Declaration** unanimously adopted
- **Summit:** **18th BRICS Summit**
- **When and where:** **September 12, 2026**, **New Delhi**
- **Status:** **Approved**
# 2. Key positions
| Area | Declaration position |
|---|---|
| Dispute resolution | **Dialogue and diplomacy**; opposition to **unilateral wars** |
| Economy and governance | Promotion of **local currencies**; **reform of global governance**; stronger **economic and strategic cooperation** |
> Exam angle: Recall the **Delhi Declaration**, its unanimous adoption at the **18th BRICS Summit**, and its key positions.

international.headline: South-South Cooperation Day highlights cooperation among developing countries
facts: The UN Day for South-South Cooperation is observed on September 12; the notes state it began in 2004.
The 2026 theme is “Solidarity Rising: Global Alliance for Inclusive and Innovative Development”.
The United Nations is the associated body; the observance focuses on economic, social and technological cooperation among developing nations.
international.summary: The day promotes cooperation among developing nations across economic, social and technological fields.
international.prelimsTakeaway: UN Day for South-South Cooperation is September 12; the listed 2026 theme is “Solidarity Rising: Global Alliance for Inclusive and Innovative Development”.
international.mainsAngle: Consider how cooperation among developing countries can support inclusive development and shared capabilities.
international.notes:
# 1. Observance
- **Name:** **UN Day for South-South Cooperation**
- **Date:** **September 12**
- **Associated body:** **United Nations**
- **First observed:** **2004**
- **Status:** **Ongoing**
# 2. Theme and objective
- **2026 theme:** “**Solidarity Rising: Global Alliance for Inclusive and Innovative Development**”
- **Objective:** **Economic, social and technological cooperation among developing nations**
> Exam angle: Match **September 12** and the **2026 theme** with the **UN Day for South-South Cooperation**.

andhraPradesh.canonicalTopic: Colombo Security Conclave Table Top Exercise 2026
andhraPradesh.headline: Colombo Security Conclave table-top exercise held in Visakhapatnam
group2: Paper I: AP History & Culture, Indian Constitution, Governance
facts: The three-day Colombo Security Conclave Table Top Exercise concluded at the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam on September 12, 2026.
Representatives from India, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Mauritius discussed coordinated responses to illegal activities at sea.
The activity was a discussion-based simulation, not a live military exercise.
The Colombo Security Conclave was established in 2020 and has its secretariat in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
andhraPradesh.summary: Participants used scenario-based discussion to consider coordinated maritime security responses.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: The Colombo Security Conclave’s focus areas include maritime security, counter-terrorism, trafficking, transnational organised crime, cybersecurity and humanitarian assistance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The exercise involved India, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Mauritius and was hosted at Visakhapatnam’s Eastern Naval Command.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate regional maritime cooperation and the role of scenario-based exercises in preparedness.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The table-top exercise was held at the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

sources.title: Colombo Security Conclave Table Top Exercise–2026 Held in Visakhapatnam

andhraPradesh.notes:
# 1. What happened
- **What:** **Three-day Colombo Security Conclave Table Top Exercise**; concluded on **September 12, 2026**
- **Type:** **Discussion-based simulation**; coordinated responses to illegal activities at sea; **not a live military exercise**
- **Venue:** **Eastern Naval Command**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**
# 2. Participants
| Participants | Country | Country |
|---|---|---|
| **Representatives** | **India**; **Sri Lanka** | **Maldives**; **Mauritius** |
# 3. Colombo Security Conclave
- **Established:** **2020**
- **Secretariat:** **Colombo, Sri Lanka**
- **Focus areas:** **Maritime security**; **counter-terrorism**; **trafficking**; **transnational organised crime**; **cybersecurity**; **humanitarian assistance**
- **AP link:** Exercise hosted at the **Eastern Naval Command**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**
- ⚠ **Trap:** **Table-top exercise** was discussion-based, not a live military exercise.
> Exam angle: Identify the **Visakhapatnam** venue, participating countries and discussion-based nature of this **Colombo Security Conclave** exercise.
